lead: Oklahoma City plumbing deals with clay soil, ice storms, severe weather and older homes near Midtown. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Oklahoma City.
risk: cracked sewer lines in clay soil, frozen pipes in ice storms and slab leaks
risk_short: sewer lines, frozen pipes and slab leaks
why: Mesta Park, Heritage Hills and Crown Heights have homes from the 1910s to the 1940s with galvanized supply lines and clay or cast-iron sewer laterals. Clay soil shrinks and swells and cracks them.
Ice storms freeze pipes in crawl spaces and exterior walls, often during power outages. Newer suburban homes sit on slabs, where leaks under the floor happen.
water: OKC draws from Lake Hefner, Lake Overholser, Lake Stanley Draper and lakes in southeast Oklahoma by pipeline. The water is moderately hard.
problems: Mesta Park, Heritage Hills and older areas
tips: Drip faucets in an ice storm.
Scope the sewer line before buying an older home.
Watch your water bill for slab leak signs.
areas: PipeMend works in Midtown, Mesta Park, Heritage Hills, the Plaza District, Crown Heights, the Paseo, Edgemere Park and every other neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the Oklahoma City Development Services Department, and plumbers must be licensed by the Oklahoma Construction Industries Board.

faq.q: Why do Oklahoma City sewer lines crack?
faq.a: Much of the city sits on clay that swells when wet and shrinks when dry. Older clay and cast-iron sewer pipes crack as the ground moves. A camera inspection shows where.
